content:
UGC Contracts and Usage Rights (2026): A Plain-English Guide

Most UGC disputes come from one missing sentence: how the brand is allowed to use the video. This guide explains usage rights, whitelisting and exclusivity in plain English, and gives you a checklist of what every UGC agreement should say. It is general information, not legal advice; for large deals, have a lawyer review the contract.

Table of Contents

1. Usage rights explained
2. Types of usage and how to price them
3. UGC contract checklist
4. A simple email agreement template
5. Disclosure rules
6. FAQ

1. Usage Rights Explained

When you make UGC, you create a video. The contract decides what the brand may do with it. The three questions are always the same: where (organic channels, paid ads, website, retail), how long (30 days, 90 days, a year, forever) and where in the world (one country, a region, worldwide).

2. Types of Usage and How to Price Them

UsageWhat the brand can doCommon pricing approach
OrganicPost on its own social accounts and websiteIncluded in the base rate
Paid usageRun your video as ads for a set periodAdd 30-50% of base per 30 days as a starting point
Whitelisting / Spark AdsRun ads from your account handleMonthly fee on top of usage
Raw footageRe-edit your clips into new adsAdd 25-50% of base
ExclusivityStop you working with competitorsPriced per month of exclusivity
Perpetual / buyoutUse forever, anywhere2-3x base, or decline

These are starting points, not rules. Full rate card and examples in the UGC rates guide.

3. UGC Contract Checklist

  • Parties: your name or business and the brand's legal name.
  • Deliverables: number of videos or photos, length, format, hooks, captioned and clean versions.
  • Deadlines: product arrival, first draft and final delivery dates.
  • Revisions: how many rounds, and what counts as a revision versus a new brief.
  • Usage: organic or paid, which channels, how long and which countries.
  • Whitelisting and exclusivity: yes or no, period and fee.
  • Payment: amount, currency, deposit, due date (net 15 or net 30) and how you are paid.
  • Kill fee: what you are paid if the brand cancels after you have filmed.
  • Product: who pays for it, and whether you keep it.
  • Portfolio rights: you may show the work in your portfolio.
  • Disclosure: how posts on your own account are labelled.

4. A Simple Email Agreement Template

Hi [Name], confirming what we agreed so we are on the same page:


- Deliverables: [2] UGC videos, [20-30] seconds, 9:16, [3] hooks each, captioned + clean versions
- Deadline: first drafts [date], final files [date], one round of revisions
- Usage: organic on [Brand] channels + paid ads for [30] days in [countries]
- Fee: [amount + currency], [50]% on signing, balance within [15] days of delivery
- Cancellation after filming: [50]% of the fee
- I can show the videos in my portfolio after they go live


Reply "confirmed" and I will get started. Thanks!

5. Disclosure Rules

If the content is posted on your own account, it is an ad and must be labelled. In the US see the FTC's disclosure guide; in the UK the ASA influencer guide; Canada and EU countries have similar rules. Content the brand posts on its own channels is the brand's responsibility to label.

Show Your Terms Upfront

Publish your rates and packages next to your samples, so brands know your usage pricing before they ask.

Build My Free UGC Portfolio

Free. No account needed. No follower minimum.

FAQ

What are usage rights in UGC?

Usage rights say where, how and for how long a brand can use your content. Organic use means the brand's own pages and accounts; paid usage means running it as ads. Paid and longer usage is worth more and is usually priced on top of the base rate.

Do I need a contract for UGC?

You need the terms in writing. A short email or a platform agreement that lists deliverables, usage, revisions, payment terms and deadlines is enough for most beginner jobs.

What is whitelisting in UGC?

Whitelisting (Spark Ads on TikTok, partnership ads on Meta) means the brand runs ads from your account handle. It uses your identity, so it is usually priced separately, often per month.

Should I give perpetual usage rights?

Only for a much higher fee. Perpetual rights let a brand use your content forever, so many creators charge two to three times their base rate or decline.
